source: ZINOS-brand-guidelines-A4.pdf (ZINOS Design Studio, Brand guidelines v1.0, November 2026, 19 pages A4)

spacing.page_margin: 39pt on A4 (13.8 mm); web equivalent 40px at 1440px, 20px on mobile
spacing.print_margins: letterhead 20 mm; 3 mm bleed; 4 mm safe margin

rules: Michroma: display and headlines only, sentence case, tracking +0 (+60 only in the wordmark)
Michroma never for numbers, prices, forms or body text
Sentence case for headings and buttons; no exclamation marks

shadows: none: depth comes from photography, never from CSS shadows
rules_and_borders: 0.75pt ink hairline as section divider (≈1px on screen)

grid.columns: 3-column body (39 / 218 / 398pt starts) with a 2-column variant split at 313pt

taste.name: Cobalt is a single word, not a theme
taste.trigger: When a layout needs a point of emphasis (a button, a card face, a cover)
taste.decision: Chose one cobalt (#2D4BFF) element per layout, carried otherwise by white and ink, over a blue-tinted UI where links, icons and headings share the accent
taste.reason: A colour that appears once reads as a decision; the eye lands on it first, so it can only point at the one thing that matters (start a project)
evidence: 'One cobalt element at most per piece' on stationery

taste.name: Wide display face kept on a short leash
taste.trigger: When choosing where the extended, technical Michroma face is allowed
taste.decision: Chose to confine Michroma to the wordmark and headlines of a few words, with DM Sans Light for everything read, over using the display face for navigation, numbers and UI labels to push the brand voice
taste.reason: Extended letterforms are memorable at 36-56px and tiring at 14px; numbers in a wide face look like a tech logo rather than a price a client can trust
evidence: 'Never numbers, prices, forms or body text'
Stationery uses no Michroma at all

taste.name: One logo, then silence
taste.trigger: When a layout has room for more brand marks (footers, watermarks, photo corners)
taste.decision: Chose one logo per layout, with the Z monogram wherever the name would repeat and no logo on photographs, over repeating the lockup as a pattern or watermark
taste.reason: A studio that sells restraint has to show it; repeated logos read as insecurity and compete with client work
evidence: Website: wordmark in nav, Z in footer, hero photo clean

taste.name: Hairlines and flat grounds instead of boxes
taste.trigger: When grouping content: contents list, personality traits, font-use table, asset inventory
taste.decision: Chose 0.75pt ink hairlines and flat fog panels with square corners, no shadows and no rounded cards, over card UI with radius and elevation
taste.reason: Ruled lists read like a printed spec sheet, which matches a studio that promises checked files; depth is left to the photography, lit by one soft source
evidence: No drop shadows anywhere in the PDF
Imagery spec: 'lit by one soft source'
